name: Facilities and workplace management
one_line: The physical workplace as an administered thing: premises and space records, floor plans and desk allocation, planned and reactive maintenance, access control and keys, workplace services and their suppliers, moves and fit-outs, and the statutory site checks that keep a place lawfully occupiable. The anchor is a SITE and its running record — the occupier's operational view of a building — which is what separates it from owning, letting, or constructing that building. Absorbs the legacy row ops.facilities-workplace. Gist-level placeholder (J-IND): it recognises the situation and writes NO field rows, because the business_operations schema declares none.

deterministic: PRECONDITION: every entry below is a DETECTION signal and never an extraction licence. The business_operations schema declares no field rows (D1 as narrowed, _CONTRACT rules 10 and 15, CONNECTION PR-6), so nothing here writes a domain fact; detection exists so the material is recognised, kept where this row's sensitivity says, and offered honestly. “Privacy policy must be enforced before content reaches any model or external connector.”
a space-record structure: a floor or area identifier crossed with an area measure, a use or department allocation, and a capacity or desk count — a plan, a schedule, or both together.

a planned-maintenance structure: an asset or plant item (lift, boiler, HVAC unit, fire alarm panel) crossed with a service frequency, a last-service date, a next-due date and a contractor. The asset-and-next-due pairing is the most characteristic table in the row. “Tables matter because resumes, forms, applications, invoices, and administrative documents often place their most useful information in cells rather than body paragraphs.”
a reactive-works structure: a helpdesk or job log with a location slot, a fault description, a priority, an attending contractor and a completion record.

a statutory-check structure: a site inspection or test certificate with a labelled premises address, a test date, a next-due date and a competent-person or engineer identification — fire risk assessment, electrical installation condition report, water hygiene, lift examination, gas safety.

an access structure: a card, key, or fob register listing holders against zones and issue and return dates, or a door-schedule and alarm-code record. This structure is simultaneously the row's most characteristic and its most sensitive.
an occupancy-services structure: a cleaning, catering, security, or reception specification or schedule keyed to a site, with hours and service standards.
a move or fit-out structure: a dated migration plan naming departments, floors, phases and a cutover date — which is a project shape wearing a facilities subject.
parent-folder context naming a site, a building, or a floor, treated as a clue once one of the structures above is present. Folder context never fires alone.
needs_llm: PRECONDITION: this world is commercially confidential and often confidential to a THIRD party, so any model step runs after P7 and under the user's policy. “Protected material should not be included in cloud-model prompts by default, should not display raw content in general group summaries, and should not be moved automatically without a user policy that explicitly permits it.”

the central determination for this row: separating the OCCUPIER's running record from the OWNER's, the LANDLORD's and the BUILDER's. A lease, a service-charge demand, a snagging list and a maintenance schedule can all name one address, and the property and construction families own three of those four.

separating a workplace record from a HOUSEHOLD one. A boiler service certificate, an alarm code note and a floor plan are identical artifacts in a home, and for a home-based business they are genuinely one file.

separating a facilities safety record from an employee safety record. A fire risk assessment is the premises'; an accident book entry is a person's, and belongs with the hr family under a stricter posture.
unlabelled facilities prose: a note about a leak, an email about parking, a memo about desk allocation with no address and no asset.

a purpose-coherent site file whose members are individually unremarkable — a plan, a certificate, three invoices, a contractor method statement and a spreadsheet of keys. “The documents are content-incoherent but purpose-coherent.”
in every case above, abstention is the required outcome where the evidence does not settle it. “A model that cannot cite sufficient evidence must return unknown.”
never_alone: a street address alone. An address appears on a lease, a delivery note, a customer record, a letterhead and a personal document equally, and reading it as a site is the tempting false conclusion for this row.

facilities vocabulary alone — site, premises, maintenance, access, workplace, inspection. Property listings, insurance guidance, hotel operations material and saved supplier brochures are dense in it.
a certificate-shaped PDF alone, which is equally an insurance certificate, a compliance certificate, a trade qualification or a personal credential.
a floor-plan-shaped drawing alone. A plan is architectural, estate-agency, construction and facilities material equally, and the drawing itself does not say which.
a date-shaped token read as a next-due date without a labelled slot.

a company, charity, or regulator gazetteer hit alone. 00 states the ambiguity for a university — “A university name alone should not create a group because Columbia can appear as an authoring school, course provider, target institution, employer, research venue, or merely a cited organization.” — and a company name is worse, appearing as employer, customer, supplier, competitor, regulator, and as the letterhead of a document that is merely ABOUT the holder. Stated as inference; 00 writes that sentence about a university, not a company.

source_type or extension alone. “treat the file extension as a routing signal rather than an assumption about meaning”, and file_kind_plausible is constitutionally never-alone (CONNECTION section 5, invariant 2).
membership in a download session that emptied a document-management system or a mail thread's attachments at once. “A session should never be treated as proof of topic”

a PDF author, producer, or company metadata string alone. “PDF metadata should be treated as supporting evidence, not as truth” — a corporate template stamps the same entity on every blank form it ever generated.
a bare 4-digit number read as a fiscal year, an entity number, a contract number, or a document version.

grouping_reasons: one site over time: its plans, certificates, maintenance schedule, works history and services. The strongest reason here and the one most likely to tempt an address label onto an unrelated PDF, which is exactly what must not happen. “The graph does not automatically copy those missing facts onto sparse files.”
one asset across its service history, joined by an asset identifier rather than by filenames.

one works occurrence: the request, the quotation, the permit, the attendance record and the invoice — purpose-coherent even where the members share no content. “The documents are content-incoherent but purpose-coherent.”
one inspection cycle: the assessment, the actions, the remedial works and the re-inspection.
one move or fit-out from plan to cutover.
no group at all is a valid outcome: a single boiler service certificate is an ordinary standalone record.

and the stop rules apply as written — “when members carry irreconcilable course, institution, project, term, or purpose facts” — two sites' records in one folder do not merge, and a home address mixed with a workplace address is the commonest real instance.

template.why: Empty by binding contract: a dimension may only branch on a field the same entry's schema declares, and business_operations declares none (D1 as narrowed, _CONTRACT rules 10 and 15, CONNECTION PR-6). That is a contract fact, not a claim that this situation has no shape — it plainly does, and it is recorded here as PROSE for whoever answers the schema row's open_question. The recommendation, held as prose: the site or building, then the asset, area, or service it concerns, then the document function, with the year only where the corpus really cycles annually. A next-due certificate is unintelligible above its asset, which is 00's own reason for putting a course above a homework number. Note that a site level is a genuine location and a location is not the collector 00's validator rejects — “use an author or organization merely as a collector” Not time-first — “For document and record domains, project, function, or subject usually comes before time because putting year first scatters related work across calendar folders.” And whatever eventually lands stays a recommendation: “The system recommends an order based on the domain template, but the user can reverse, remove, add, or flatten dimensions.”

collides_with.signal: The load-bearing collision on this row. Occupier and landlord records name one address and share inspections, works and service records. The discriminating evidence is TENURE: a lease, a rent demand, a service-charge apportionment, a dilapidations schedule, or a tenant-management framing supports the property row; the occupier's own space plan, asset register, maintenance schedule and access records support this row. Provenance: inference.

The instrument version of the same confusion. A lease is the property family's; the occupier's obligations extracted FROM it into a maintenance and inspection calendar are this row's. Provenance: inference.

Common-parts maintenance, statutory inspections and contractor management are byte-identical. The discriminating evidence: a leaseholder or resident body, a service-charge budget, or a demised-versus-common-parts framing supports block management; a single occupier's own workplace supports this row. Provenance: inference.

A fit-out is a construction project and a facilities move at once. The discriminating evidence: a works contract, valuations, variations and a snagging list support the construction row; a department migration plan, desk allocation and a cutover date support this row. Provenance: inference.

Safety is split here on WHO is at risk. The discriminating evidence: material identifying employees — an accident report, an occupational health record, a personal DSE assessment — is the hr row and must be protected before any model path; an assessment of the PREMISES supports this row. Provenance: inference.

Asset registers overlap almost completely, and a door-access system is both an IT asset and a facilities control. The discriminating evidence: a device, licence, or endpoint identifier supports the IT row; a fixed plant item tied to a building supports this row. Provenance: inference.

Cleaning, security and maintenance contracts are administered as contracts and consumed as services. The discriminating evidence: a register entry, a notice date and an obligation tracker support contract administration; the operational schedule, job log and site record supports this row. Provenance: inference.

A trading premises' opening checks, cleaning rotas and maintenance logs are this row's shape in a sector with its own trading rules. The discriminating evidence is a trading, licensing, or guest-facing anchor, which supports the sector row. Provenance: inference.

For a home-based holder the same boiler certificate, alarm record and floor plan are household material. The discriminating evidence is whether the record concerns a workplace occupied by an organisation or a dwelling occupied by a household, and for a home office it is genuinely undecidable — abstention is the correct outcome: “Correct abstention is a successful outcome because the product’s goal is reliable organization, not maximum file movement.” Provenance: inference.

falls_through_to.why: Access registers, keyholder details and alarm codes are authentication material, and site incident records name individuals; the protective home is correct for them. “Protected Records may represent sensitive isolated material such as passport scans, medical documents, account statements, visas, legal forms, or credentials; it should normally remain local-only and must not cause filenames or content to be exposed in model prompts.”

The commonest home for a standalone certificate, inspection report or service record with no site file around it. “Independent Records may live under Personal/Independent Records and hold standalone certificates, notices, confirmations, forms, and PDFs that have a durable purpose but no broader group.”

The honest outcome for a site-shaped document whose address, tenure, or side is unresolved. “Review Later may hold files whose meaning is partly understood but whose final location requires a future decision.”

Isolated works invoices, delivery notes and supplier confirmations with no job around them. “Receipts and Confirmations may hold isolated invoices, delivery confirmations, booking records, boarding passes, purchase receipts, event tickets, and similar transactional documents.”

Site condition and defect photographs with no report, group, or project association. “One-Off Images may live under Photos/One-Off Images and hold images with no event, project, reference collection, or photo-family association.”

Supplier brochures, saved specifications and model policies are the tempting false files of this row. “Reference Clips may live under Personal/Reference Clips and hold saved visual inspiration, product references, quotes, recipes, short article captures, code snippets, or other material that is useful for later retrieval but does not belong to a current project.”

CAD files, proprietary building-management exports and password-protected site packs are ordinary here and are safest represented without moving. “Unsupported or Encrypted may hold—or, more safely, represent without moving—password-protected archives, unreadable documents, damaged files, and unknown formats.”

sensitivity_why: Most of this row is dull and a small, identifiable part of it is not. Access card registers, keyholder lists and alarm codes are authentication material — 00 requires exactly that class to be protected at once: “A scanned passport, tax statement, medical document, authentication key, or account record should enter a protected state immediately.” — and its corpus sentence names both credentials and GPS metadata among what the corpus holds: “can include identity documents, account statements, tax records, medical information, legal records, credentials, private correspondence, GPS metadata, employment materials, and educational records”, which reaches this row through site photographs. Site incident and access records also name individuals, including contractors and visitors who are not the user. Because the sensitive members are indistinguishable from the dull ones by filename, the cautious setting is the honest one for the row as a whole. This row assigns only the catalogue value potentially_sensitive; the handling class is P7's and is not set here.
open_question: Two. (1) The occupier-versus-owner boundary with the construction_property family is drawn here on TENURE, and it is defensible but was drawn by this pass: an owner-occupier holds both sets of records for one address and the split then produces two rows for one folder. R1c should confirm the tenure discriminator or replace it. (2) The workplace-versus-household boundary is genuinely undecidable for a home-based holder, and it is not an edge case in a personal-file product — it may be the majority case. This row's provisional posture is abstention rather than a guess from the address, and whether that is acceptable, or whether a home-office situation deserves its own recognition, is Joseph's call.
